{{short description|Isotope geochemistry modelling method}}
In [[stable isotope geochemistry]], the '''Urey–Bigeleisen–Mayer equation''', also known as the '''Bigeleisen–Mayer equation''' or the '''Urey model''',<ref name="liu2010">{{cite journal | last1 = Liu | first1 = Q. | last2 = Tossell | first2 = J.A. | last3 = Liu | first3 = Y. | title = On the proper use of the Bigeleisen–Mayer equation and corrections to it in the calculation of isotopic fractionation equilibrium constants | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 74 | issue = 24 | year = 2010 | pages = 6965–6983 | doi = 10.1016/j.gca.2010.09.014| bibcode = 2010GeCoA..74.6965L }}</ref> is a model describing the approximate equilibrium [[isotope fractionation]] in an isotope exchange reaction.<ref name="richet1977">{{cite journal | last1 = Richet | first1 = P. | last2 = Bottinga | first2 = Y. | last3 = Javoy | first3 = M. | title = A Review of Hydrogen, Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, Sulphur, and Chlorine Stable Isotope Fractionation Among Gaseous Molecules | journal = Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences | year = 1977 | volume = 5 | pages = 65–110 | doi = 10.1146/annurev.ea.05.050177.000433 | bibcode = 1977AREPS...5...65R}}</ref><ref name="young2015">{{cite journal | last1 = Young | first1 = E.D. | last2 = Manning | first2 = C.E. | last3 = Schauble | first3 = E.A. | display-authors = etal | title = High-temperature equilibrium isotope fractionation of non-traditional stable isotopes: Experiments, theory, and applications | journal = Chemical Geology | year = 2015 | volume = 395 | pages = 176–195 | doi = 10.1016/j.chemgeo.2014.12.013| bibcode = 2015ChGeo.395..176Y }}</ref><ref name="dauphas2016">{{cite journal | last1 = Dauphas | first1 = N. | last2 = Schauble | first2 = E.A. | title = Mass Fractionation Laws, Mass-Independent Effects, and Isotopic Anomalies | journal = Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences | volume = 44 | pages = 709–783 | year = 2016 | doi = 10.1146/annurev-earth-060115-012157 | bibcode = 2016AREPS..44..709D| doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="blanchard2017">{{cite journal | last1 = Blanchard | first1 = M. | last2 = Balan | first2 = E. | last3 = Schauble | first3 = E.A. | title = Equilibrium Fractionation of Non-traditional Isotopes: a Molecular Modeling Perspective | journal = Reviews in Mineralogy and Geochemistry | year = 2017 | volume = 82 | issue = 1 | pages = 27–63 | doi = 10.2138/rmg.2017.82.2| bibcode = 2017RvMG...82...27B | s2cid = 100190768 | url = https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-02108218/file/Chapter2_revised.pdf }}</ref><ref name="li2021">{{cite journal | last1 = Li | first1 = L. | last2 = He | first2 = Y. | display-authors = etal | title = Nitrogen isotope fractionations among gaseous and aqueous NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>, NH<sub>3</sub>, N<sub>2</sub>, and metal-ammine complexes: Theoretical calculations and applications | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 295 | year = 2021 | pages = 80–97 | doi = 10.1016/j.gca.2020.12.010| bibcode = 2021GeCoA.295...80L | s2cid = 233921905 | url = http://dspace.imech.ac.cn/handle/311007/86061 }}</ref> While the equation itself can be written in numerous forms, it is generally presented as a ratio of [[Partition function (statistical mechanics)|partition functions]] of the isotopic molecules involved in a given reaction.<ref name="urey1947">{{cite journal | last = Urey | first = H.C. | title = The Thermodynamic Properties of Isotopic Substances | journal = Journal of the Chemical Society | year = 1947 | pages = 562–581 | doi = 10.1039/JR9470000562 | pmid = 20249764}}</ref><ref name="bigeleisen1947">{{cite journal | title = Calculation of Equilibrium Constants for Isotopic Exchange Reactions | last1 = Bigeleisen | first1 = J. | last2 = Mayer | first2 = M.G. | journal = The Journal of Chemical Physics | volume = 15 | issue = 5 | year = 1947 | pages = 261–267 | doi = 10.1063/1.1746492 | bibcode = 1947JChPh..15..261B| hdl = 2027/mdp.39015074123996 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> The Urey–Bigeleisen–Mayer equation is widely applied in the fields of [[quantum chemistry]] and [[geochemistry]] and is often modified or paired with other quantum chemical modelling methods (such as [[density functional theory]]) to improve accuracy and precision and reduce the [[Computational complexity|computational cost]] of calculations.<ref name="liu2010" /><ref name="li2021" /><ref name="iron2019">{{cite journal | last1 = Iron | first1 = M.A. | last2 = Gropp | first2 = J. | title = Cost-effective density functional theory (DFT) calculations of equilibrium isotopic fractionation in large organic molecules | journal = Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics | volume = 21 | issue = 32 | pages = 17555–17570 | year = 2019 | doi = 10.1039/C9CP02975C| pmid = 31342034 | bibcode = 2019PCCP...2117555I | s2cid = 198491262 }}</ref>

The equation was first introduced by [[Harold Urey]] and, independently, by [[Jacob Bigeleisen]] and [[Maria Goeppert Mayer]] in 1947.<ref name="richet1977" /><ref name="urey1947" /><ref name="bigeleisen1947" />

== Description ==
Since its original descriptions, the Urey–Bigeleisen–Mayer equation has taken many forms. Given an isotopic exchange reaction <math>A+B^*=A^*+B</math>, such that <math>^*</math> denotes a molecule containing an isotope of interest, the equation can be expressed by relating the [[equilibrium constant]], <math>K_{{eq}}</math>, to the product of [[Partition function (mathematics)|partition function]] ratios, namely the [[Translational partition function|translational]], [[Rotational partition function|rotational]], [[Vibrational partition function|vibrational]], and sometimes electronic partition functions.<ref name="urey1935">{{cite journal | last1 = Urey | first1 = H.C. | last2 = Greiff | first2 = L.J. | title = Isotopic Exchange Equilibria | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | volume = 57 | issue = 2 | date = 1935 | pages = 321–327 | doi = 10.1021/ja01305a026}}</ref><ref name="bigeleisen1975">{{cite book | last = Bigeleisen | first = J. | chapter = Quantum Mechanical Foundations of Isotope Chemistry | title = Isotopes and Chemical Principles | editor-last = Rock | editor-first = P.A. | volume = 11 | series = ACS Symposium Series | date = 1975 | pages = 1–28 | isbn = 978-0-8412-0225-2 | doi = 10.1021/bk-1975-0011.ch001}}</ref><ref name="he2018">{{cite thesis | last = He | first = Y. | date = 2018 | type = PhD thesis | title = High-dimensional isotope relationships | chapter = Equilibrium intramolecular isotope distribution in large organic molecules | pages = 48–66 | chapter-url = https://digitalcommons.lsu.edu/gradschool_dissertations/4695 | publisher = Louisiana State University}}</ref> Thus the equation can be written as: <math>K_{eq} = \frac{[A^*][B]}{[A][B^*]}</math> where <math>[A]=\prod^n Q_{n,A}</math> and <math>Q_n</math> is each respective partition function of molecule or atom <math>A</math>.<ref name="he2018" /><ref name="li2011">{{cite journal | last1 = Li | first1 = X. | last2 = Liu | first2 = Y. | title = Equilibrium Se isotope fractionation parameters: A first-principles study | date = 2011 | journal = Earth and Planetary Science Letters | volume = 304 | issue = 1 | pages = 113–120 | doi = 10.1016/j.epsl.2011.01.022| bibcode = 2011E&PSL.304..113L }}</ref> It is typical to approximate the rotational partition function ratio as quantized [[rotational energy|rotational energies]] in a [[rigid rotor]] system.<ref name="bigeleisen1975" /><ref name="webb2013">{{cite journal | last1 = Webb | first1 = M.A. | last2 = Miller | first2 = T.F. III | title = Position-Specific and Clumped Stable Isotope Studies: Comparison of the Urey and Path-Integral Approaches for Carbon Dioxide, Nitrous Oxide, Methane, and Propane | journal = J. Phys. Chem. A | date = 2013 | volume = 118 | issue = 2 | pages = 467–474 | doi = 10.1021/jp411134v | pmid = 24372450 | url = https://authors.library.caltech.edu/43327/| url-access = subscription }}</ref> The Urey model also treats [[molecular vibration]]s as simplified [[harmonic oscillator]]s and follows the [[Born–Oppenheimer approximation]].<ref name="bigeleisen1975" /><ref name="webb2013" /><ref name="liu2021">{{cite journal | title = Theoretical calculation of position-specific carbon and hydrogen isotope equilibriums in butane isomers | last1 = Liu | first1 = Q. | last2 = Yin | first2 = X. | last3 = Zhang | first3 = Y. | display-authors = etal | journal = Chemical Geology | volume = 561 | date = 2021 | article-number = 120031 | doi = 10.1016/j.chemgeo.2020.120031| bibcode = 2021ChGeo.56120031L | s2cid = 230547059 }}</ref>

Isotope partitioning behavior is often reported as a '''reduced partition function ratio''', a simplified form of the Bigeleisen–Mayer equation notated mathematically as <math>\frac{s}{s'}f</math> or <math>(\frac{Q^*}{Q})_r</math>.<ref name="ishida1969">{{cite book | last1 = Ishida | first1 = T. | last2 = Spindel | first2 = W. | last3 = Bigeleisen | first3 = J. | chapter = Theoretical Analysis of Chemical Isotope Fractionation by Orthogonal Polynomial Methods | title = Isotope Effects in Chemical Processes | pages = 192–247 | doi = 10.1021/ba-1969-0089.ch011 | series = Advances in Chemistry | year = 1969 | volume = 89 | isbn = 978-0-8412-0090-6}}</ref><ref name="rosenbaum1997">{{cite journal | last = Rosenbaum | first = J.M. | title = Gaseous, liquid, and supercritical fluid H<sub>2</sub>O and CO<sub>2</sub>: Oxygen isotope fractionation behavior | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 61 | issue = 23 | date = 1997 | pages = 4993–5003 | doi = 10.1016/S0016-7037(97)00362-1 | bibcode = 1997GeCoA..61.4993R }}</ref> The reduced partition function ratio can be derived from [[power series]] expansion of the function and allows the partition functions to be expressed in terms of frequency.<ref name="ishida1969" /><ref name="oneil1986">{{cite book | last = O'Neil | first = J.R. | chapter = Theoretical and experimental aspects of isotopic fractionation | title = Stable Isotopes in High Temperature Geological Processes | publisher = De Gruyter | date = 1986 | doi = 10.1515/9781501508936-006 | series = Reviews in Mineralogy & Geochemistry | volume = 16}}</ref><ref name="yang2018">{{cite web | last = Yang | first = J. | title = Mass-Dependent Fractionation from Urey to Bigeleisen | website = Department of Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences | publisher = Massachusetts Institute of Technology | date = 2018 | url = https://jeehyuny.github.io/MDF_JY.pdf | url-status = live | archive-date = 26 December 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221226183841/http://jeehyun.scripts.mit.edu/jeehyn/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Mass-Dependent-Fractionation-Jeehyun-Yang.pdf}}</ref> It can be used to relate molecular vibrations and intermolecular forces to equilibrium isotope effects.<ref name="bigeleisen1973">{{cite journal | last1 = Bigeleisen | first1 = J. | last2 = Lee | first2 = M.W. | last3 = Mandel | first3 = F. | title = Equilibrium Isotope Effects | journal = Annual Review of Physical Chemistry | date = 1973 | volume = 24 | pages = 407–440 | doi = 10.1146/annurev.pc.24.100173.002203| bibcode = 1973ARPC...24..407B }}</ref>

As the model is an approximation, many applications append corrections for improved accuracy.<ref name="liu2021" /> Some common, significant modifications to the equation include accounting for pressure effects,<ref name="polyakov1994">{{cite journal | last1 = Polyakov | first1 = V.B. | last2 = Kharlashina | first2 = N.N. | title = Effect of pressure on equilibrium isotopic fractionation | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 58 | issue = 21 | pages = 4739–4750 | date = 1994 | doi = 10.1016/0016-7037(94)90204-6| bibcode = 1994GeCoA..58.4739P }}</ref> nuclear geometry,<ref name="bigeleisen1996">{{cite journal | last = Bigeleisen | first = J. | title = Nuclear Size and Shape Effects in Chemical Reactions. Isotope Chemistry of the Heavy Elements | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | date = 1996 | volume = 118 | issue = 15 | pages = 3676–3680 | doi = 10.1021/ja954076k}}</ref> and corrections for [[anharmonicity]] and quantum mechanical effects.<ref name="liu2010" /><ref name="richet1977" /><ref name="bigeleisen1998">{{cite journal | last = Bigeleisen | first = J. | title = Second-order correction to the Bigeleisen–Mayer equation due to the nuclear field shift | journal = PNAS | volume = 95 | issue = 9 | date = 1998 | pages = 4808–4809 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.95.9.4808 | pmid = 9560183 | pmc = 20168 | bibcode = 1998PNAS...95.4808B | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="prokhorov2019">{{cite journal | last1 = Prokhorov | first1 = I. | last2 = Kluge | first2 = T. | last3 = Janssen | first3 = C. | title = Optical clumped isotope thermometry of carbon dioxide | journal = Scientific Reports |  volume = 9 | number = 4765 | date = 2019 | page = 4765 | doi = 10.1038/s41598-019-40750-z | doi-access = free| pmid = 30886173 | pmc = 6423234 | bibcode = 2019NatSR...9.4765P }}</ref> For example, [[Hydrogen–deuterium exchange|hydrogen isotope exchange reactions]] have been shown to disagree with the requisite assumptions for the model but correction techniques using [[Path integral formulation|path integral methods]] have been suggested.<ref name="liu2010" /><ref name="bigeleisen1947" /><ref name="webb2017">{{cite journal | last1 = Webb | first1 = M.A. | last2 = Wang | first2 = W. | last3 = Braams | first3 = B.J. | display-authors = etal | title = Equilibrium clumped-isotope effects in doubly substituted isotopologues of ethane | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 197 | date = 2017 | pages = 14–26 | doi = 10.1016/j.gca.2016.10.001| bibcode = 2017GeCoA.197...14W | url = https://authors.library.caltech.edu/71374/1/1-s2.0-S0016703716305671-main.pdf }}</ref>

== History of discovery ==
One aim of the [[Manhattan Project]] was increasing the availability of concentrated radioactive and stable isotopes, in particular [[Carbon-14|<sup>14</sup>C]], [[Sulfur-35|<sup>35</sup>S]], [[Phosphorus-32|<sup>32</sup>P]], and [[deuterium]] for [[heavy water]].<ref name="manhattan1">{{cite journal | title = Availability of Radioactive Isotopes | journal = Science | volume = 103 | issue = 2685 | pages = 697–705 | date = 14 June 1946 | doi = 10.1126/science.103.2685.697| pmid = 17808051 | bibcode = 1946Sci...103..697. }}</ref> [[Harold Urey]], Nobel laureate physical chemist known for his discovery of deuterium,<ref name="urey1932">{{cite journal | last1 = Urey | first1 = H.C. | last2 = Brickwedde | first2 = F.G. | last3 = Murphy | first3 = G.M. | title = A Hydrogen Isotope of Mass 2 | journal = Phys. Rev. | year = 1932 | volume = 39 | issue = 1 | pages = 164–165 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.39.164| bibcode = 1932PhRv...39..164U | doi-access = free }}</ref> became its head of isotope separation research while a professor at [[Columbia University]].<ref name="uchicago_urey">{{cite web | title = Guide to the Harold C. Urey Papers 1932-1953 | date = 2007 | website = University of Chicago Library | url = https://www.lib.uchicago.edu/e/scrc/findingaids/view.php?eadid=ICU.SPCL.HCUREY | access-date = 25 December 2022}}</ref><ref name="hewlett1962">{{cite book | title = The New World, 1939/1946 | series = A History of the United States Atomic Energy Commission | volume = I | date = 1962 | last1 = Hewlett | first1 = R.G. | last2 = Anderson | first2 = O.E. | publisher = The Pennsylvania State University Press | chapter = In the beginning | pages = 9–52 | url = https://www.governmentattic.org/5docs/TheNewWorld1939-1946.pdf}}</ref>{{rp|45}} In 1945, he joined [[Enrico Fermi Institute|The Institute for Nuclear Studies]] at the University of Chicago, where he continued to work with chemist [[Jacob Bigeleisen]] and physicist [[Maria Goeppert Mayer|Maria Mayer]], both also veterans of isotopic research in the Manhattan Project.<ref name="bigeleisen1975" /><ref name="uchicago_urey" /><ref name="nas_bigeleisen">{{cite web | title = Jacob Bigeleisen: 1919–2010 | website = National Academy of Sciences | series = Biographical Memoirs | date = 2014 | url = https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/bigeleisen-jacob.pdf}}</ref><ref name="nobel_mayer">{{cite news | title = Maria Goeppert Mayer - Biographical | website = The Nobel Prize | url = https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1963/mayer/biographical/}}</ref> In 1946, Urey delivered the [[Liversidge Award|Liversidge lecture]] at the then-[[Royal Institute of Chemistry]], where he outlined his proposed model of stable isotope fractionation.<ref name="richet1977" /><ref name="urey1947" /><ref name="bigeleisen1975" /> Bigeleisen and Mayer had been working on similar work since at least 1944 and, in 1947, published their model independently from Urey.<ref name="richet1977" /><ref name="bigeleisen1947" /><ref name="bigeleisen1975" /> Their calculations were mathematically equivalent to a 1943 derivation of the reduced partition function by German physicist [[Ludwig Waldmann]].<ref name="bigeleisen1947" /><ref name="bigeleisen1975" />{{efn|Bigeleisen & Mayer (1947) contains the addendum:''{{blockquote|After this paper had been completed, Professor [[Willard Libby|W.F. Libby]] kindly called a paper by L. Waldmann<ref name="waldmann1943">{{cite journal | last = Waldmann | first = L. | title = Zur Theorie der Isotopentrennung durch Austauschreaktionen | language = German | trans-title = On the theory of isotope separation by exchange reactions | journal = Naturwissenschaften | volume = 31 | pages = 205–206 | date = 1943 | issue = 16–18 | doi = 10.1007/BF01481918| bibcode = 1943NW.....31..205W | s2cid = 20090039 }}</ref> to our attention. In this paper, Waldmann discusses briefly the fact that the chemical separation of isotopes is a quantum effect. He gives formulae which are equivalent to our (11') and (11a) and discusses qualitatively their application to two acid-base exchange equilibria. These are the exchange between NH<sub>3</sub> and NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> and HCN and CN<sup>–</sup> studies by Urey<ref name="thode1939">{{cite journal | last1 = Thode | first1 = H.G. | last2 = Urey | first2 = H.C. | title = The Further Concentration of N<sup>15</sup> | journal = J. Chem. Phys. | volume = 7 | pages = 34–39 | doi = 10.1063/1.1750320 | date = 1939| issue = 1 | bibcode = 1939JChPh...7...34T | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="hutchison1940">{{cite journal | last1 = Hutchison | first1 = C.A. | last2 = Stewart | first2 = D.W. | last3 = Urey | first3 = H.C. | title = The Concentration of C<sup>13</sup> | journal = J. Chem. Phys. | volume = 8 | pages = 532–537 | date = 1940 | issue = 7 | doi = 10.1063/1.1750707| bibcode = 1940JChPh...8..532H }}</ref> and co-workers.}}''}}

== Applications ==
Initially used to approximate chemical [[reaction rate]]s,<ref name="urey1947" /><ref name="bigeleisen1947" /> models of isotope fractionation are used throughout the [[physical sciences]]. In [[chemistry]], the Urey–Bigeleisen–Mayer equation has been used to predict [[Equilibrium constant#Effect of isotopic substitution|equilibrium isotope effects]] and interpret the distributions of isotopes and [[isotopologue]]s within systems, especially as deviations from their [[natural abundance]].<ref name="ishida2002">{{cite journal | last = Ishida | first = T. | title = Isotope Effect and Isotope Separation: A Chemist's View | journal = Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology | date = 2002 | volume = 39 | issue = 4 | pages = 407–412 | doi = 10.1080/18811248.2002.9715214| bibcode = 2002JNST...39..407I | s2cid = 95785450 }}</ref><ref name="saunders2014">{{cite journal | title = Calculation of Equilibrium Isotope Effects in a Conformationally Mobile Carbocation | last1 = Saunders | first1 = M. | last2 = Cline | first2 = G.W. | last3 = Wolfsberg | first3 = M. | journal = [[Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A]] | year = 1989 | volume = 44 | issue = 5 | pages = 480–484 | doi = 10.1515/zna-1989-0518| bibcode = 1989ZNatA..44..480S | s2cid = 95319151 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The model is also used to explain [[isotopic shift]]s in [[spectroscopy]], such as those from nuclear field effects or [[Mass-independent fractionation|mass independent effects]].<ref name="liu2010" /><ref name="bigeleisen1996" /><ref name="ishida2002" /> In biochemistry, it is used to model [[enzyme|enzymatic]] [[kinetic isotope effect]]s.<ref name="moiseyev1997">{{cite journal | last1 = Moiseyev | first1 = N. | last2 = Rucker | first2 = J. | last3 = Glickman | first3 = M.H. | title = Reduction of Ferric Iron Could Drive Hydrogen Tunneling in Lipoxygenase Catalysis: Implications for Enzymatic and Chemical Mechanisms | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | date = 1997 | volume = 119 | number = 17 | pages = 3853–3860 | doi = 10.1021/ja9632825}}</ref><ref name="gropp2021">{{cite journal | last1 = Gropp | first1 = J. | last2 = Iron | first2 = M.A. | last3 = Halevy | first3 = I. | journal = Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta | volume = 295 | date = 2021 | pages = 237–264 | doi = 10.1016/j.gca.2020.10.018 | title = Theoretical estimates of equilibrium carbon and hydrogen isotope effects in microbial methane production and anaerobic oxidation of methane| bibcode = 2021GeCoA.295..237G | url = https://chemrxiv.org/engage/api-gateway/chemrxiv/assets/orp/resource/item/60c7518a567dfe1bd8ec5a95/original/theoretical-estimates-of-equilibrium-carbon-and-hydrogen-isotope-effects-in-microbial-methane-production-and-anaerobic-oxidation-of-methane.pdf }}</ref> [[Model-based testing|Simulation testing]] in [[computational systems biology]] often uses the Bigeleisen–Mayer model as a [[Baseline (science)|baseline]] in the development of more complex [[Modelling biological systems|models of biological systems]].<ref name="wong2015">{{cite journal | last1 = Wong | first1 = K.Y. | last2 = Xu | first2 = Y. | last3 = Xu | first3 = L. | title = Review of computer simulations of isotope effects on biochemical reactions: From the Bigeleisen equation to Feynman's path integral | journal =  Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Proteins and Proteomics| volume = 1854 | issue = 11 | date = 2015 | pages = 1782–1794 | doi = 10.1016/j.bbapap.2015.04.021| pmid = 25936775 }}</ref><ref name="giese2022">{{cite journal | last1 = Giese | first1 = T.J. | last2 = Zeng | first2 = J. | last3 = Ekesan | first3 = S. | last4 = York | first4 = D.M. | title = Combined QM/MM, Machine Learning Path Integral Approach to Compute Free Energy Profiles and Kinetic Isotope Effects in RNA Cleavage Reactions | journal = J. Chem. Theory Comput. | date = 2022 | volume = 18 | issue = 7 | pages = 4304–4317 | doi = 10.1021/acs.jctc.2c00151 | pmid = 35709391 | pmc = 9283286 | url = https://theory.rutgers.edu/resources/pdfs/acs.jctc.2c00151.pdf}}</ref> Isotope fractionation modeling is a critical component of [[isotope geochemistry]] and can be used to reconstruct [[paleoecology|past Earth environments]] as well as examine [[Geomorphology|surface processes]].<ref name="kendall1998">{{cite book | title = Isotope Tracers in Catchment Hydrology | editor-last1 = Kendall | editor-first1 = C. | editor-last2 = McDonnell | editor-first2 = J.J. | date = 1998 | publisher = Elsevier Science B.V. | last1 = Kendall | first1 = C. | last2 = Caldwell | first2 = E.A. | chapter = Chapter 2: Fundamentals of Isotope Geochemistry | url = https://wwwrcamnl.wr.usgs.gov/isoig/isopubs/itchinfo.html | chapter-url = https://wwwrcamnl.wr.usgs.gov/isoig/isopubs/itchch2.html}}</ref><ref name="otake2008">{{cite thesis | last = Otake | first = Tsubasa | type = PhD thesis | title = Understanding Redox Processes in
